clues: This city sits in a wide valley where two rivers flow together into one. Low, flat land spreads out from the banks on each side.
Summer heat here can be fierce, but a sea breeze can cool the night fast. Folks call that cool wind the delta breeze.
In 1852, this city lent its court house to the state lawmakers for their work. Two years later, it was made the state capital for good.
In 1848, a man struck gold at a mill on a stream near here. Thousands of gold hunters rushed in, and the small town boomed.
The laws of the state are made in this city, in its capitol. The governor of California works here too.
